Where to Buy Nintendo Switch Games Cheapest in 2026

Roundup · Updated 2026-08-07

First-party Nintendo Switch games almost never drop below full price at the eShop, so "cheapest" usually comes down to where you shop and whether you buy physical or digital. Here's how the main stores stack up in 2026, and the fastest way to grab a given title for less.

Amazon — best all-rounder for physical carts

For boxed Switch games, Amazon is usually the cheapest mainstream option and the easiest to price-track. Prime members get free shipping, and third-party sellers often undercut Nintendo's own MSRP on older titles. It's our default pick for physical cartridges.

Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on Amazon Tears of the Kingdom on Amazon Animal Crossing on Amazon

Nintendo eShop — digital convenience, rare discounts

Buying digitally means no cartridge to lose and instant downloads, but the eShop rarely discounts first-party games outside its seasonal sales (usually spring, summer, and Black Friday). If you want digital, wait for those events or stack eShop gift-card deals (see our budget games guide).

GameStop & Walmart — trade-in credit and clearance

GameStop's trade-in credit can quietly beat cash prices if you have old games to swap, and Walmart's Rollback pricing sometimes undercuts Amazon on mega-popular titles during holidays. Both are worth a quick check before a big purchase.

Used & resale — cheapest per cart, with caveats

eBay and local marketplaces are where cartridges get cheapest, especially for games a year or two old. The catch: you're buying a used cart only (no download code, no return window), and prices move with demand. Great for back-catalogue picks, less so for brand-new releases.

Green Man Gaming & other key shops

GMG and similar key shops are fantastic for PC and some PlayStation titles, but Nintendo locks its eShop ecosystem tight — physical Switch carts basically never appear there. Don't waste time hunting Switch keys on those sites; stick to the retailers above.

Best time to buy

If a game is less than six months old, expect to pay near MSRP everywhere. The real savings show up around Black Friday, the Nintendo eShop seasonal sales, and the slow fade of last year's hits into the used market. For a specific title, set a price alert rather than buying on launch day.

Our pick for most buyers

Want it now and want it cheap? Grab the physical cartridge on Amazon. Want it forever on your console and don't mind paying a little more? Wait for an eShop sale. Either way, avoid paying full eShop price on day one for a game that's been out a while.
